_comment: lib_trans -- the 43 adjudicated-translate outward callees (LIB-TRANS), the last game logic the
migrated modules still call in the original binary. Decomposed 2026-09-02; the numbers and the
why live in docs/lib-trans-closure.md.
WHY THE MEMBERSHIP IS A FROZEN NAME LIST AND NOT A LIVE QUERY OVER THE ADJUDICATION LEDGER.
The obvious selector -- 'every libmh_call_ledger.json callee classed translate' -- is
SELF-UNDERMINING by the domain's own burn-down design: when a callee gains a verified
migration-ledger row, gen_libmh_calls --check demands its adjudication row's REMOVAL (the
orphan gate), so a live query would drop each member the moment it completes, taking its
recorded state with it -- the name_prefix failure mode, mechanized. The list below is the
translate class as adjudicated at freeze time (43 names, LIB0's ledger, 2026-09-01 state).
A NEW translate-classed callee (a translation introducing a new mh::call:: into unadjudicated
territory turns the census gate red first) is ADOPTED by editing this list explicitly --
visible, like net_session's third-member rule, not silently absorbed.
THE PRNG DOCTRINE REVERSAL, stated so nobody reads it as an accident: every other profile
carries llm_rand in frontier_prefixes ('its state is shared with every un-migrated consumer,
so reimplementing it buys nothing'). That was true while the goal was minimising live seams;
LIB-REF changes the goal -- the RNG family runs ON THE REPLAY PATH, so standalone libmh cannot
exist without owning it. The hazard the frontier rule guarded against is retired by HOW we
translate: the bodies keep binding _G_LLM_STRAT_RNG_STATE / the channel state at its original
region (D1 layout freeze), and promotion is an E9 at the original entry, so every un-migrated
consumer self-heals into ours -- one state, one implementation, never two. The D-E4 landmine
stands: llm_rand (Watcom CRT, cosmetic/tactical) and llm_strat_rng_next (the sim LCG, already
ours) are TWO RNGs and stay two; nothing in this domain touches the CRT one.
THE UNSHADOWABLE PAIR (llm_strat_frame, llm_strat_frame_redraw_behind_dialog) is batch F and
verification-special: both ADVANCE THE SIM (pump + time_tick + sim_tick), so a shadow arm
would double-step the world -- no shadow site, ever. They are also tiny (86 + 72 B): pure
orchestrators whose callees are either already ours (pump, sim_tick, time_tick) or
host-callback walls (input_update, render_present, render_view). Their evidence is the
composite A/B the -P runs: with the pair promoted, every determinism oracle exercises OUR
frame spine end-to-end.
title: The adjudicated-translate outward callees

select.walk_why: The seeds ARE the answer, but for a different reason than sim_resid's: this domain's closure instrument is the CENSUS, not a graph walk. Translating a member whose callee is original and previously unreferenced creates a new mh::call:: site, which lands in libmh_call_census.json as a new callee, which the LIB0 lint refuses until adjudicated -- a red gate at exactly the moment the edge becomes real, stronger than a static walk's guess in advance. The walk preview (docs/lib-trans-closure.md sect. 4) was still computed and classified so the likely adoptions are named before they happen.

seeds.why: MEMBERSHIP FROZEN 2026-09-02: the libmh_call_ledger.json translate class as adjudicated by LIB0 (43 callees, ~7.9 KB), frozen as names because the live query self-empties through the orphan gate (see _comment). The two settled exclusions are LIB0's, restated so nobody re-adds them: llm_strat_input_update was RECLASSED mixed/walled (SIM-RESID-W walls it; the replay host replaces the input pump; decomposition is post-fork), and the host-callback / cfg-snapshot / crt / dead classes are NOT translation work by adjudication. ADOPTED 2026-09-02 (wave-2 census): game_RemoveFromAvailableBuildings + game_RemoveFromAvailableProjects -- the Progress/Available writers llm_progress_finalize_acquire (b2) reaches; the closure doc's predicted-adoption path, adopted by editing this list explicitly per the rule above.

select.effect_prefixes_why: sim_resid's wall list plus the presentation/sound targets this domain's own out-edges measurably reach (cam_set_col/row, race_alert text+sound emit, group_order_ack_voice, render_present/render_view via the frame pair, dlg_build_from_table via menu_force_return). Declared as effect_prefixes because walk is none -- there is no closure to cut; the list drives the shadow-safety inventory: an outward call into one of these fires TWICE per armed call while the state comparison reads clean.

paths._module_dir_why: The sim_resid pattern: a subdirectory of mh/sim (same namespace, same state interface, own .cpp tree so the ledger diff does not interleave with sim's rows). DEFAULT destination only -- the roster spans owners (the lockstep-side rows: player_by_side_id, peer_timing_reset, reload_snapshot_resync_clocks; the ai-called RNG draws), and LT-PREP owns the per-row destination decision; a row re-homed into mh/lockstep binds through THAT module's interface instead, recorded in its ledger row's notes. lint_repo's sim raw-address check globs libmh/sim/ and covers the default tree unchanged.
paths._effect_classes_why: SIM'S SHARED FILE, sim_resid's reason verbatim: gen_dll_effects.py installs a gate over an ADDRESS, so two domains that both reach llm_snd_play cannot each own its class -- the generator refuses a name two domains classify differently. This domain's new effectful targets (race_alert emits, ack_voice, cam_set pair, dlg_build_from_table, render_present/view, chat_target_add) get classified INTO the shared file at LT0.

items._interface_why: LT0 is deliberately thin: the state interfaces are REUSED (sim's for the default tree, lockstep's for re-homed rows -- the sim_resid reasoning: these bodies write the same regions through the same stores, and a second store over one region set is the two-bindings hazard). What LT0 OWNS is the delta: binding the regions this domain writes that no interface carries yet (RNG channel state, diplomacy relations, progress/available tables, the map-region pool + block cursor, invasion-alert sentinels, ambient event times, peer timing), the libtranstest oracle, and classifying the new effect targets into the shared file. Every batch deps LT0 directly, which is what lint_migration_items checks.

_ns_why: Read by translate.js as the writer-brief default; mh::sim is the majority destination. A batch whose rows LT-PREP re-homes into mh/lockstep must pass that module's ns/state_header in its fan-out args instead of inheriting this default -- the TACT1A fail-open lesson; batch D's item carries the reminder.

oracle._selftest_why: Its own registered suite (net_selftest libtranstest), built at LT0, exercising all 43 rows through the EXISTING module fixtures rather than a new store binding (the fixture classes are shared scaffolding; the sim_resid two-fixtures hazard is about a second region-binding store, which this suite must not create). One suite = one gate = one number for the umbrella's burn-down; the alternative -- scattering cases across simtest/aitest/lockstest -- leaves the domain's oracle status unreadable. LT0 may still delegate individual cases to a module suite where the fixture genuinely cannot be reached from a shared file; if so the ledger row names the suite that covers it.

rig._why: Split population, so `sp` default with `soak` for the per-tick rows: the session/boot rows (diplomacy inits, seeds, deploy_starting_squad, cfg_final_planet_Construct, peer_timing_reset) run ONCE per run -- a soak buys nothing for them (sim_resid's lesson) -- while the RNG draws, time_GetCurrentTime, invasion_alert_poll, prod_transfer_progress and the cursor helpers are per-tick/per-frame and reach T3 only on a run with real traffic. player_by_side_id and reload_snapshot_resync_clocks need MP shapes (lockstep message handlers / resync) -- their sites take zero calls in sp, which the anti-vacuity rule reports only after the run is spent; check a row's callers before ordering a rig run.

rules.why: THE UNSHADOWABLE PAIR (llm_strat_frame + llm_strat_frame_redraw_behind_dialog -- one prefix catches both). Listed first because 'frame' vocabulary could bleed into other rules. Translate LAST: their callees must already be ours or walled, and their evidence is composite (see _comment).

THE DETERMINISTIC RNG FAMILY -- rand_below/ai/fx, state_advance, seed_ch0/ch1. First because it is the domain's calibration batch: rand_below has 13 original callers and fires constantly, so its shadow site produces a real armed differential (T3) cheaply, calibrating the offline oracle before the once-per-session rows have to be trusted on T2. Smallest bodies in the domain (31-59 B each); the D-E4 two-RNGs landmine is this batch's one hazard.

THE PROGRESS/INVENTION ENGINE -- the six llm_progress_* bodies plus game_ClearAvailableProjects and game_UpdatePlanetProgress. One closed family over Progress[]/AvailableProjects with its sinks (game_HandleProgress, game_UpdateProgress, game_SetEvent) ALREADY TRANSLATED -- intra-family edges become direct C++ calls (G21). Contains the domain's one self-recursion (finalize_acquire recurses over system planets) and three order_queue_dispatch-reached rows (0xee/0xc dispatch), so orders traffic exercises it. (AvailableBuildings added 2026-09-02 for the two adopted Remove* rows.)

MAP-REGION POOL + PLACEMENT GRIDS -- region_free, region_pool_reset, block_8_GetNextBlock (the pool allocator), setup_dimensions, scan_masked_table_for_empty_cell, bldg_recompute_cell_grid. Deterministic segmentation/placement state; callers sit in map build/load paths, so the offline oracle carries most of the evidence. CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (LT-PREP dig): the AI construction scanners consume the passable[] plane via scan_masked_table_for_empty_cell, NOT bldg_recompute_cell_grid's derived grid -- that grid has NO CONFIRMED READER (4-method sweep; see its ledger row note) and may resolve `dead` at batch time.

SESSION/BOOT + THE LOCKSTEP-SIDE ROWS -- the once-per-run writers (diplomacy tables, peer timing, planet clone, starting squad, ambient event reseed) plus the lockstep query player_by_side_id and the desync-path flow control force_return_to_main. The domain's whole effect surface outside batch F lives here (snd_play + cam_set in deploy_starting_squad; the alert/ack emits in reload_snapshot_resync_clocks; dlg_build_from_table in force_return; chat_target_add in diplomacy_init_multiplayer) -- so this batch gates on the effect classes being authored. Rows LT-PREP re-homes into mh/lockstep get that module's ns/state_header in the fan-out args, not this profile's mh::sim default. ambient_reseed calls rand_below_fx (batch A) -- direct C++ once both are ours, hence the item's dep on LT1A.

SMALL HELPERS AND QUERIES -- the math pair, str_char_subst, prod_transfer_progress, the soldier-slot query, the two placement-table helpers facing_step_apply + squad_placement_offset_lookup (renamed at the domain close from llm_ui_cursor_*; soldier coords despite the old ui name), time_GetCurrentTime (pure derived read of the sim clock, 24 callers incl. 17 tact), the invasion-alert pair, cfg_GetAnimTime. Mostly pure or single-region writers; per-tick callers give several of them T3 reach.

_conductor_owned_why: sim_resid's list plus this domain's own adjudication surfaces: a translation writer that could edit libmh_call_ledger.json or libmh_call_census.json could adjudicate its own new outward call or fake the burn-down the umbrella's done_when is measured on -- the same self-certification hazard as writer_dispositions.json. lib_trans_selftest.cpp is the oracle; the orders_issue rule applies (a writer must not author the expectations its own translation is graded against beyond its per-row cases).
_non_autonomous_why: LIB-TRANS is the umbrella and holds no work of its own. LT-PREP is human-driven Ghidra work plus the per-row destination-module decision. LT0 edits shared conductor-owned interfaces and adjudicates effect classes -- both conductor-only by this profile's own list. LT1F is the unshadowable pair: no per-call oracle exists, its evidence is a composite A/B a human has to read. LIB-TRANS-P decides what runs for real on an asymmetric determinism run. LT-READY and batches A-E are loop-drivable once LT0 lands.
